findings.description: SHEET-PUB-001's phrasing names two distinguishable activities ('republish' and 'the periodic mark-refresh') that must share 'one serialized loop, never concurrently.' All three A-outputs independently and convergently read this as: two separately-triggerable job kinds (Republish from event-append/on-demand; MarkRefresh from a timer) funneled into a single-consumer async channel/actor (tokio mpsc + one `run()` loop) so they structurally cannot race. The real code has no such job-type split at all: every trigger site — TUI connect (`LivePort::connect`), manual `[r]` (`run_refresh`), the hourly ambient tick (`shell::should_autorefresh` in `tui_app.rs` event_loop), the deferred post-submit refresh, and the headless `pt summary` path (`run_headless_summary` → `run_live_cycle`) — calls the exact same fused function, `runtime::run_cycle_publishing` / `sheets_view::Publisher::republish_then_settle` (cycle.rs:428-435, lib.rs:1012-1025), which ALWAYS does write-then-read as one atomic synchronous call. There is no 'mark-refresh only' code path, no channel, no async runtime anywhere in these files — the whole system is single-threaded/synchronous (a poll-based TUI loop or a one-shot CLI process), so 'never concurrently' is a structural byproduct of there being only one fused operation, not a scheduling guarantee over two independently-arriving job types.

The actual serialization mechanism is not an in-process scheduler at all (as every A-run assumed) but a cross-process advisory WRITE lock (`pt_core::Lock` / `runtime::AdvisoryLock`, guarding against a separate OS process — e.g. a concurrently-run `pt summary` — touching the same workbook), and critically the lock covers ONLY the write half: `Publisher::republish` (lib.rs:954-999) acquires the lock immediately before the first `batch_update_view` and the guard drops before the function returns; the settle/mark-refresh read (`read_price_pass` via `read_marks`) then ALWAYS runs afterward, completely unlocked, and UNCONDITIONALLY — even when the write half reported `published:false` because the lock was `Held` or a tab write failed (`republish_then_settle`, lib.rs:1012-1025, calls `read_marks` regardless of `outcome`). All three B-runs converge on exactly this (B1 'Ubiquitous — lock scope' + 'held lock'; B2 point 3; B3 U2/S2); no A-run modeled a lock, a cross-process concern, or 'settle proceeds regardless of write outcome' — spec text gives no basis for any of it.

Held-lock refusal is a fully non-destructive silent no-op, not a wait/queue/error: under a `Held` (or erroring) lock, `republish` writes NO tabs, leaves the current stale set unchanged byte-for-byte, and reports `published:false` for that cycle only, relying entirely on the next trigger to retry (`republish_under_a_held_lock_writes_nothing` in republish.rs:239-254 pins this). Spec text is silent on what happens when the 'never concurrently' constraint is actually contended — this specific non-destructive-refusal contract is pure code-side surplus, agreed on identically by B1, B2, and B3.

Republish's failure granularity is per-tab, not per-job: each of the five bands (Positions/Open Lots/Realized/Tax-accrual/Tax-reserve-summary) is its own atomic `batchUpdate`; one tab's failure flags only that tab stale in a persistent `BTreeSet` (retried next cycle), writes a best-effort single-cell banner of the exact text `"STALE — last sync {ts}"` (itself allowed to fail silently — `write_stale_banner`), and does NOT abort republishing the remaining tabs; the workbook tab order is then unconditionally reasserted regardless of any individual tab's outcome (lib.rs:973-999). SHEET-PUB-001 treats 'republish' as a single verb with no such internal structure — all three B-runs reconstruct this identical granularity, down to the exact banner string.

All three A-outputs explicitly leave the mark-refresh period as an externally-injected, unspecified `Duration` ('no default chosen here' / 'external config input') since the spec states no value. The real code hardcodes it as a fixed constant, `shell::AUTOREFRESH_INTERVAL` (tui_app.rs:184-188), not threaded through as configuration, and additionally suppresses the ambient tick entirely while an entry composer is open, deferring it to the first tick after the composer closes (`event_loop`, tui_app.rs:244-246) — a conditional-periodicity nuance no A-run or the spec text anticipates.

notes:
Read all six real files in full (tui_app.rs, wiring.rs, cycle.rs, publish_cycle.rs, sheets-view/src/lib.rs, sheets-view/tests/republish.rs) before classifying.

Excluded as assumption artifacts (unanimous across A1/A2/A3, no spec-text basis, therefore NOT counted as findings per the instructions): the tokio/mpsc/channel/actor realization itself; bounded-vs-unbounded channel and try_send-coalescing-vs-no-coalescing choices; the oneshot on-demand ack (A2 only) and explicit Shutdown variant (A3 only); 'log and continue on failure' as the crash policy. These are real inventions but none trace to explicit SHEET-PUB-001 text, so per the classification rules they don't count as A-side findings on their own — I folded the one part of them that DOES trace to spec text (the implied two-distinguishable-job-types shape) into BD finding #1 instead of listing the mechanism (tokio) as a finding.

Also present in the B-runs but treated as out-of-scope noise for SHEET-PUB-001 specifically (not listed as findings): the settle-poll degrade rules (`SettleConfig::max_polls` default 8, `DegradeReason::{TimedOut,Permanent,SubCent}`, `price_to_cents`'s round-half-to-even/SCALE=1_000_000 rule, offline-propagation/prior-carry contract on `read_marks`). These are real, heavily-detailed code-side surplus, but they almost certainly belong to a sibling EARS area (marks/settle, e.g. SHEET-MARK-*) rather than the republish-timing/serialization requirement (SHEET-PUB-001) that's being audited here — all three B-runs reconstruct them near-identically, which is why bAgreement is rated high despite this being a large chunk of their combined output.

Classification rationale: this is BD-DRIFT rather than B-ONLY or A-ONLY because the two directions aren't independently silent/noisy — they triangulate on the SAME underlying gap. The spec's wording ('republish AND the periodic mark-refresh... never concurrently') straightforwardly reads as describing two independently-schedulable activities needing a coordination mechanism, which is exactly what all three A-outputs built (unprompted, and consistently). The B-outputs then reveal what the coordination mechanism actually is in the real code — and it's structurally nothing like what A built: no two job types, no channel, no in-process scheduler; instead a single fused write-then-read function called synchronously from every trigger site, with the only real (cross-process) concurrency protection coming from an advisory lock that deliberately covers just the write half. That's a direct, well-attested (high agreement on both sides) mismatch between what the spec's phrasing invites an implementer to build and what the real system actually does.
